question: Should accepted hooks reloads use this process-global transform-generation boundary for concurrent in-flight webhook deliveries, or should reload state be scoped more narrowly to each resolved hooks runtime snapshot?
rationale: The patch intentionally chooses a runtime-state lifecycle contract rather than merely correcting a local import cache; the supplied evidence proves the intended normal and rejected-candidate cases but does not establish the desired product semantics for every in-flight delivery boundary.

options.title: Accept generation-scoped cache lifecycle
options.body: Approve the current design if it is acceptable that accepted reloads establish the transform-module generation used by subsequently started loads across the gateway process.

options.title: Scope cache state to resolved hook snapshots
options.body: Ask for a snapshot-owned cache design if each in-flight delivery must remain bound to the exact hooks runtime accepted when that delivery began.

recommendation.title: Accept generation-scoped cache lifecycle
recommendation.body: Approve the current design if it is acceptable that accepted reloads establish the transform-module generation used by subsequently started loads across the gateway process.

likelyOwner.reason: This is the only identified person connected to the current implementation in the supplied evidence; a current-main gateway-history owner should be added during maintainer review.
